title: Choose the visual world for Executive Admin
question: The roll assigned Receiving Stamp. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Receiving Stamp
options.lineage: Philippine office rubber stamps, stamp-pad ink and dry seals: RECEIVED, FOR APPROVAL, APPROVED, dated by hand
options.thesis: Every status is a stamp mark the whole office already reads at a glance.
materials: stamp-pad violet, red and blue inks
options.viewport: A ruled form-sheet shell: a stamped app mark, a numbered nine-drawer sidebar, and each page's Coming Soon set as a dated receiving stamp.
options.risk: Turns into costume if stamps are tilted or textured past legibility; marks must stay straight and crisp.

raised.raise: One ruling grammar: every rule, border and divider is a one-pixel hairline drawn on the same form grid; no shadows or soft cards.
Every module carries a form number (EA-04.2 Shell Fleet Cards), so navigation, breadcrumbs and search speak one code.
Registry columns are fixed and only their values change; status restyles a row without moving the grid.

options.label: Routing Slip
options.lineage: the stapled For Approval routing slip with a signature-and-date box per approver
options.thesis: The app is the routing slip: every request shows its chain of boxes, signed or waiting.
options.viewport: A sidebar of form sections and a content sheet headed by a horizontal row of approval boxes.
options.risk: The familiar, safe office-form reading; close to what most admin tools in this category already look like.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.lineage: international airport sign system, yellow overhead bands
options.thesis: Nine groups as signed concourses; each page shows only the decisions ahead.
options.viewport: A yellow sign band carries breadcrumbs and the next decision, with gate-style module numbers.
options.case: Strong on clarity of navigation; loses on audience identification for a corporate back office.
options.risk: Yellow at page scale is fatiguing for all-day operators.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Two dense columns around a keyed centre rail.
options.viewport: Twin text columns with a vermilion key rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: operators don't identify with scholarly apparatus.
options.kept: One-device-pixel ruling discipline across every rule.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Every item a coded cell in a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: A packed grid of coded cells keyed to a map.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no imagery to fill cells in an admin app.
options.kept: Every module carries a code that navigation and search share.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Rows as live entities on a fixed board.
options.viewport: A black departures board of requests.
options.case: Fuses partly: fits renewals, but the dark board fights a daytime office.
options.risk: All-caps condensed type hurts long reading.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.viewport: A vertical staff of shaded blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract notation hides status.
options.risk: Needs a legend to read anything.
options.kept: Exactness: dates and stages always shown exactly, never vaguely.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.case: Fuses as a generic admin; nothing the audience recognizes as theirs.
options.kept: Accent rationed to a handful of uses per screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean neutral SaaS admin shell, Linear/Vercel style, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Collapsible grey sidebar, top bar with search, centered empty state.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin panel by design.
